newsitem.title: USA: IMF denies rumors of delay in Russia negotiations.
newsitem.headline: IMF denies rumors of delay in Russia negotiations.

text.p: The International Monetary Fund denied rumors on Thursday that Russia had asked for a delay in negotiations on its 1997 economic program.
"We have not been informed that the Rusian government has asked for, nor is it intending to ask for, a delay in the negotiations on the 1997 program," an IMF spokesman said.

Rumors about a possible delay arose after First Deputy Prime Minister Vladimir Potanin was quoted as saying that Russia would ask the IMF for a respite of several months to decide how to restructure its natural monopolies.
"An IMF mission intends to commence work next week with a view for completing discussions on the 1997 program as soon as possible," the spokesman said in a statement.
"In the context of these discussions," the spokesman added," the timing of various measures that have been under consideration will be finalized."
The discussions are taking place under a $10 billion loan deal between the Fund and Russia.
